<a> Hyperlink Anchor Element HTML Tags

✔ WITH <a> Expected Behavior & Feature

Provides native browser hyperlinking, allowing one-click transitions between the live dispatch console and the comprehensive technical dictionary.

✖ WITHOUT <a> Visible Flaw / Impact if Omitted

<aside> Sidebar Container Element HTML Tags
Encloses secondary navigation, branding, and app links docked to viewport edge.

Role in Project Udaan

Renders docked obsidian navigation dock, keeping brand emblem and navigation persistent on screen.

Code Usage Pattern

<aside class="sidebar">...</aside>
✔ WITH <aside> Expected Behavior & Feature

Establishes a persistent, high-contrast obsidian dock (width: 240px) pinned to the left screen edge, grouping brand emblem, module navigation, and architect profile with semantic <aside> landmark accessibility.

✖ WITHOUT <aside> Visible Flaw / Impact if Omitted

Without <aside>, the sidebar falls into the main document body stream. Screen readers cannot bypass navigation, and CSS fails to isolate the left dock from central operational consoles, causing the entire 3-column layout to collapse into a single stacked column.

<body> Document Body Root HTML Tags
Contains all visual DOM nodes rendered on screen in standard HTML5 mode.

Role in Project Udaan

Houses the entire application canvas and establishes base typography and linen cream backdrop.

Code Usage Pattern

✔ WITH <body> Expected Behavior & Feature

Initializes the full-viewport canvas with zero margin/padding, Plus Jakarta Sans font smoothing, and the warm linen cream background (#FAF7F2).

✖ WITHOUT <body> Visible Flaw / Impact if Omitted

<button> Interactive Action Trigger HTML Tags

fsmClaim() Transition State: OPEN -> IN_PROGRESS JS Functions
Advances active grievance ticket along the FSM directed graph, assigning it to field engineer V. K. Saxena.

Role in Project Udaan

Executes data structure logic and updates live DOM telemetry for 'fsmClaim()'.

Code Usage Pattern

function fsmClaim() { ticket.transitionState(LifecycleState::IN_PROGRESS); }
✔ WITH fsmClaim() Expected Behavior & Feature

Advances grievance from OPEN to IN_PROGRESS, assigns field engineer V. K. Saxena, updates the state badge, and logs engineer dispatch in telemetry.

✖ WITHOUT fsmClaim() Visible Flaw / Impact if Omitted

Without 'fsmClaim()', tickets remain stuck in OPEN indefinitely; field work cannot begin, and the issue can never be transitioned toward resolution.

fsmResolve() Transition State: IN_PROGRESS -> RESOLVED JS Functions
Marks field engineering works as physically resolved, recording resolution timestamp and telemetry.

Role in Project Udaan

Executes data structure logic and updates live DOM telemetry for 'fsmResolve()'.

Code Usage Pattern

function fsmResolve() { ticket.transitionState(LifecycleState::RESOLVED); }
✔ WITH fsmResolve() Expected Behavior & Feature

Validates that the ticket is currently IN_PROGRESS, transitions it to RESOLVED, logs repair completion, and prepares the ticket for citizen democratic audit.

✖ WITHOUT fsmResolve() Visible Flaw / Impact if Omitted

Without 'fsmResolve()', field engineers cannot mark works complete; tickets remain perpetually in progress, distorting resolution statistics.

fsmVerify() Transition State: RESOLVED -> VERIFIED JS Functions
Executes closed-loop democratic verification by the original citizen complainant, completing audit loop.

Role in Project Udaan

Executes data structure logic and updates live DOM telemetry for 'fsmVerify()'.

Code Usage Pattern

function fsmVerify() { ticket.transitionState(LifecycleState::VERIFIED); }
✔ WITH fsmVerify() Expected Behavior & Feature

Enforces closed-loop democratic verification by requiring citizen confirmation before final closure, preventing fraudulent resolution claims.

✖ WITHOUT fsmVerify() Visible Flaw / Impact if Omitted

Without 'fsmVerify()', the accountability loop is broken; corrupt officials could mark incomplete repairs as resolved without citizen confirmation.

26-Way Prefix Trie O(L) Data Structure: 26-Way DSA Models
Character-by-character search tree offering O(L) prefix lookup where L is query length, completely independent of total indexed keywords.

Role in Project Udaan

Drives instant search suggestions across municipal taxonomies, enabling citizens to quickly locate correct complaint categories.

Code Usage Pattern

class TrieNode { TrieNode* children[26]; bool isEndOfWord; };
✔ WITH 26-Way Prefix Trie O(L) Expected Behavior & Feature

Delivers instantaneous prefix matching in O(L) character steps (sub-microsecond), scaling seamlessly even if municipal taxonomies grow to millions of words.

✖ WITHOUT 26-Way Prefix Trie O(L) Visible Flaw / Impact if Omitted

Without the Prefix Trie, searching requires linear scans across all database strings (O(N × M)), causing noticeable UI stutter and high server load.

Inverted Keyword Hash Map O(1) Data Structure: Inverted DSA Models
Unordered associative container mapping normalized grievance summary terms to active ticket IDs for O(1) duplicate grievance detection.

Role in Project Udaan

Prevents duplicate ticket generation when multiple citizens report the same incident (e.g. water main burst on Ring Road).

Code Usage Pattern

std::unordered_map<std::string, std::vector<int>> invertedMap;
✔ WITH Inverted Keyword Hash Map O(1) Expected Behavior & Feature

Detects duplicate grievance submissions in O(1) average time, preventing redundant emergency dispatches for already-reported incidents.

✖ WITHOUT Inverted Keyword Hash Map O(1) Visible Flaw / Impact if Omitted

Without the Inverted Index, checking for duplicates requires pairwise string comparisons across all open tickets (O(N^2)), causing severe database degradation.

Anti-Sybil Unordered Hash Set O(1) Data Structure: Anti-Sybil DSA Models
Cryptographically hashed set storing validated citizen voter IDs, delivering strictly enforced single-vote per ticket in O(1) average time.

Role in Project Udaan

Guarantees democratic voting integrity, preventing botnets and malicious actors from artificially inflating grievance priority.

Code Usage Pattern

std::unordered_set<std::string> sybilVault; if (!sybilVault.insert(voterId).second) throw DuplicateVoteException();
✔ WITH Anti-Sybil Unordered Hash Set O(1) Expected Behavior & Feature

Mathematically guarantees 1-citizen 1-vote integrity by checking voter hash tokens in O(1) average time, intercepting fraud instantly.

✖ WITHOUT Anti-Sybil Unordered Hash Set O(1) Visible Flaw / Impact if Omitted

Without the Anti-Sybil Set, malicious users or automated scripts can vote repeatedly, artificially manipulating emergency priorities.

Binary Max-Heap Priority Queue O(log N) insert, O(1) peek Data Structure: Binary DSA Models
Complete binary tree satisfying the max-heap property: parent priority score is always greater than or equal to child priority scores.

Role in Project Udaan

Orders critical municipal emergencies (severity × upvotes) so the most dangerous hazards are dispatched immediately.

Code Usage Pattern

std::vector<GrievanceTicket> heap; void push(GrievanceTicket t) { /* heapify up O(log N) */ }
✔ WITH Binary Max-Heap Priority Queue O(log N) insert, O(1) peek Expected Behavior & Feature

Guarantees O(1) peek at the most critical emergency and O(log N) insertion/extraction, enforcing the Zero FIFO Latency Invariant for life-threatening hazards.

✖ WITHOUT Binary Max-Heap Priority Queue O(log N) insert, O(1) peek Visible Flaw / Impact if Omitted

Without the Max-Heap (e.g. using a standard FIFO queue), a critical gas leak lodged at 10:00 AM would wait behind 50 minor graffiti complaints lodged earlier.

Lifecycle Finite State Machine (FSM) Directed Graph Data Structure: Lifecycle DSA Models
Deterministic finite automaton enforcing legitimate state transitions: OPEN -> IN_PROGRESS -> RESOLVED -> VERIFIED.

Role in Project Udaan

Prevents state-skipping fraud (e.g. marking a ticket resolved without being claimed) and guarantees constituent audit verification.

Code Usage Pattern

enum class State { OPEN, IN_PROGRESS, RESOLVED, VERIFIED }; bool transition(State from, State to);
✔ WITH Lifecycle Finite State Machine (FSM) Directed Graph Expected Behavior & Feature

Mathematically prevents illegal state transitions (e.g. OPEN -> RESOLVED without engineer assignment) and guarantees closed-loop democratic verification.

✖ WITHOUT Lifecycle Finite State Machine (FSM) Directed Graph Visible Flaw / Impact if Omitted

Without the FSM, corrupt operators could fabricate high resolution stats by marking unresolved emergencies as 'resolved' without verification.

0/1 Knapsack Dynamic Programming O(N × B) Data Structure: 0/1 DSA Models
Dynamic programming algorithm determining optimal subset of welfare projects to fund under municipal budget constraint B.

Role in Project Udaan

Maximizes community poverty reduction (MPI delta) while strictly respecting fiscal budget limits without fractional compromises.

Code Usage Pattern

int dp[N+1][B+1]; for (int i=1; i<=N; ++i) { for (int w=0; w<=B; ++w) { if (weight[i] <= w) dp[i][w] = max(dp[i-1][w], dp[i-1][w-weight[i]] + val[i]); else dp[i][w] = dp[i-1][w]; } }
✔ WITH 0/1 Knapsack Dynamic Programming O(N × B) Expected Behavior & Feature

Achieves mathematically provable global maximum poverty reduction under fiscal constraint B with zero wasted budget and zero fractional compromises.

✖ WITHOUT 0/1 Knapsack Dynamic Programming O(N × B) Visible Flaw / Impact if Omitted

Without 0/1 Knapsack DP, budgets are allocated greedily or arbitrarily, leaving unallocated capital deficits or funding low-impact projects.

Fenwick Tree / Binary Indexed Tree (BIT) O(log W) Data Structure: Fenwick DSA Models
Implicit binary indexed tree supporting O(log W) point updates and prefix sum range queries across municipal grain distribution reserves.

Role in Project Udaan

Tracks real-time food grain stock distributions across 20 wards, allowing instant verification of regional food security quotas.

Code Usage Pattern

void update(int idx, int val) { for (; idx <= W; idx += idx & -idx) tree[idx] += val; } int query(int idx) { int sum = 0; for (; idx > 0; idx -= idx & -idx) sum += tree[idx]; return sum; }
✔ WITH Fenwick Tree / Binary Indexed Tree (BIT) O(log W) Expected Behavior & Feature

Executes stock updates and multi-ward prefix sum range queries in O(log W) time using bitwise isolation (idx & -idx), preventing grain distribution bottlenecks.

✖ WITHOUT Fenwick Tree / Binary Indexed Tree (BIT) O(log W) Visible Flaw / Impact if Omitted

Without the Fenwick Tree, multi-ward cumulative grain audits require linear scans (O(W)); updating and auditing 20 wards creates severe database lock contention.
